title: Correct acceleration calculation
description: Essential: Student correctly computes the acceleration as -g sinθ, yielding -5 m/s².

title: Velocity at 1 second
description: Important: Student applies the kinematic equation v = v₀ + at to find the velocity at t=1s.

title: Momentum at 1 second
description: Essential: Student correctly calculates the momentum at t=1s as p = m*v, yielding 2.5 kg·m/s.

title: Velocity at 3 seconds
description: Important: Student applies the kinematic equation to find the velocity at t=3s, noting its sign.

title: Change in momentum
description: Essential: Student correctly computes Δp = p_final - p_initial for the 3-second interval, yielding -7.5 kg·m/s.

title: Sign error in acceleration
description: Pitfall: Student uses a positive acceleration, ignoring the decelerating effect of gravity.

title: Momentum sign confusion
description: Pitfall: Student treats momentum as a scalar or misinterprets the negative sign in the final velocity.

title: Unit consistency
description: Optional: Student explicitly includes correct units (kg·m/s) in all final answers.
